provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
In the original task, the picture is the largest 4-connected non-background component. It is cropped to its bounding box. Each isolated two-cell domino lists a new colour first and an old colour second, reading left to right. The rule recolours every cell of the old colour in the original crop to the new colour, all at the same time.

The factory works out where the original left-to-right vector (0,+1) points in the visible grid. A row reversal (d4>=4) negates it to (0,-1). Each clockwise rotation then maps a displacement (dy,dx) to (dx,-dy). The emitted program uses the constant (DY,DX) directly. For any size-2 component whose cells differ by exactly that vector, the cell at the tail is the replacement colour and the cell at the head is the colour being replaced. Dominoes that run along other axes are ignored, which matches the native filter for horizontal dominoes only.

The background is the constant palette[0], since original black maps to it. The remap is a dictionary lookup on the unmodified crop, so newly written colours are never remapped again. No grid rotation and no un-permuting of colours take place.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the constructor's domain. The picture is a solid rectangle of at least 16 cells, so it is strictly the largest component and its bounding box contains no background. The generator's margin-1 overlap check keeps the dominoes from touching the picture or each other. Rites and lefts are disjoint distinct colours, so each old colour has at most one domino. If several aligned dominoes ever shared an old colour, the last one in scan order would win; the generator never produces that case. No contradictions with the fixtures and no constructor defects were found.

independent_source_review.mechanism: Crop the largest 4-connected non-background component, which is the solid picture rectangle, to its bounding box. Each isolated size-2 component is a legend domino. When its two cells differ by the augmented 'original left-to-right' vector (DY,DX), the tail colour replaces the head colour. All replacements are applied at once through a dictionary lookup on the unmodified crop.
evidence: Picture is always strictly the largest component and never contains background. The constructor draws `pattern` as a full wide x tall rectangle, with wide and tall in 4..7, so it is at least 16 cells. It is filled with bgcolor and rite colours from 1..9 and contains no 0. Dominoes are exactly 2 cells. So the solver's crop by `max(comps, key=len)` plus bounding box reproduces `output` exactly.

Nothing touches anything else. `common.overlaps(..., spacing=1)` requires a gap of at least one row or one column between every pair of boxes (picture plus dominoes). No domino is 4-adjacent to the picture or to another domino, so each domino is its own size-2 component. Distinct `prows` adds further separation.

Colours are unambiguous. `colors` is a shuffle of 1..9 popped without replacement, so bgcolor, lefts and rites are pairwise distinct. Each old colour has exactly one domino. The frame colour and left colours are never remapped. `cmap[rite]=left` matches the solver's `mapping[old]=new`.

Every rite colour appears in the pattern. This is guaranteed by `len(set(flatten(grid))) == num_colors + 1`. So every domino visibly acts in demonstrations, and the colour that appears inside the picture identifies the head/old side.
Output values are lookups on the original crop (`mapping.get(v, v)` over `crop`). There is no chaining. This matches the constructor's per-cell `cmap[c] if c in cmap else c`.

The factory specialises only a genuine rule direction and the background colour. The base vector is (0,1), it is negated under reflection (d4>=4), and it is rotated with the clockwise map (dy,dx)->(dx,-dy). BG is palette[0]. The solver runs directly on visible coordinates, with no whole-grid untransform or native solve.

Host audit passed: 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks, 16 fixture variants, and no sampler rejections. This is consistent with the d4 vector convention being correct. A wrong direction would skip or invert dominoes in odd-rotation variants.
Fixtures agree with the archived rule in all 4 train pairs and the test pair. For example, test dominoes 2 3, 4 8 and 6 7 give 3->2, 8->4 and 7->6, matching the given output.
nonblocking_limits: If two aligned dominoes shared an old colour, the last one in scan order would win. This is unreachable because rites are distinct.
Size-2 components not aligned with (DY,DX) are ignored. This matches the native horizontal-only filter, and the constructor emits only horizontal dominoes.
The empty-component fallback, which returns the grid unchanged, is out of domain. The constructor always places a picture.

The rule is self-contained per input via the legend. There are no cross-episode arbitrary colour associations, and the only taught constant is the domino orientation, which every demonstration exhibits.
required_context_checks: Confirm that the host D4 convention is 'reflect rows when d4>=4, then apply d4%4 clockwise quarter-turns', matching build_program's vector transform. The passed audit with 8000 augmented checks (seed d4=7) supports this.
Confirm that palette[0] is the image of original background colour 0 under the host colour permutation.

host_review.resolution: Reviewed constructor invariants, visible-coordinate solver, fixture agreement and documented out-of-domain branches. Source hashes match passing audit.
host_review.augmentation_evidence: All eight D4 transforms are checked in audit; d4=7 is its final loop index. Palette is bijective and shared across all episode pairs.
host_review.limitations: Finite execution/domain evidence, not proof of unrestricted generalization or complete identifiability.
